lines.text: Choosing insurance yourself.
Everyone in the Netherlands must have insurance for health care costs [zorgkosten]: health insurance [zorgverzekering].
A health insurer [zorgverzekeraar] pays your costs in health care.
Adults must pay a premium [premie].
You may choose your own health insurance and switch to another zorgverzekeraar every year before 1 January.
There are websites to compare [vergelijken] health insurance policies.
Choices with health insurance:
The basic insurance [basisverzekering] is mandatory for everyone.
It pays, for example, for the huisarts, the hospital, most medicines, care around pregnancy [zwangerschap] and birth, elderly care, district/home nursing [wijkverpleging] and mental health care.
Supplementary insurance [aanvullende verzekering] is not compulsory; you pay an extra premium and get back, for example, part of the physiotherapist's costs or glasses.
Dental insurance [tandartsverzekering] is separate and not compulsory.
Deductible.
You have a mandatory deductible/excess [eigen risico]: you pay part of the costs yourself.
If you choose a higher eigen risico, you pay less premium, but more costs yourself.
Example: Ricardo chose € 385 eigen risico, Merve chose € 885 and got a € 180 discount [korting] on her premium.
For an operation of € 3,000 Ricardo pays € 385 himself and Merve € 885 — in total Merve paid much more.
The eigen risico can be paid in instalments/spread out [gespreid].
For a visit to the huisarts you pay no eigen risico — that is always free.
Personal contribution.
The personal/own contribution [eigen bijdrage] is not the same as eigen risico.
For some medicines you pay an eigen bijdrage; you cannot choose this, the zorgverzekeraar decides.
Example: glasses cost € 260, the insurance pays € 150, you pay € 110 yourself — even if your eigen risico has already been paid.
Children up to eighteen.
For children up to eighteen years old, health insurance is free.
Dental insurance is also free, and you get the costs of physiotherapy reimbursed.
Zorgtoeslag.
Some people get part of the premium back from the Dutch tax authority [Belastingdienst] — the health care allowance/benefit [zorgtoeslag].
The less money you earn [verdient] per month, the more you get back.
Contact with the zorgverzekeraar.
Not sure whether the insurer will pay for a treatment?
Call or email before you start, otherwise you may get a high bill [rekening].
Most bills are sent by the huisarts or the hospital directly to the zorgverzekeraar.
Sometimes you pay yourself first, for example at the dentist; then you can claim/submit the costs for reimbursement [declareren] — online, via the app (logging in with DigiD) or by post.
Mantelzorg.
Do you care for someone for a longer period of time, for example an elderly parent or a partner or child with an illness or disability [handicap]?
That is called informal care by family/friends [mantelzorg].
Sometimes you can get compensation/reimbursement [vergoeding] for it: a personal care budget [persoonsgebonden budget, PGB].
You apply for it via the gemeente or the zorgverzekeraar.
